design.summary: All four faults are real and I traced each to an exact line. (1) The AA Battery is excluded from BOTH intercept layers for two different reasons: areaSam() requires proj==="missile" (correct — a 40mm gun is not an area SAM) and closeInGuns() bails on `e.kind !== "unit"`, which throws out every fixed mount even though the land Phalanx, Skyshield and MANTIS ARE emplacements; that second exclusion is the bug, and the profile grading already in layer 3 (x1.00 skim/cruise, x0.70 loft, x0.15 ballistic) is the right split for a gun, so I changed the eligibility test and no numbers. (2) Confirmed: every pact submarine in the game is diesel-electric (Whiskey, Foxtrot, Kilo, Improved Kilo, Varshavyanka, and sub_p) — the hole was invisible because NATO's `sub` role IS its SSN line. I added a second role, `ssn`, pact-only, across all six bands (November 1958, Victor I 1967, Akula I 1984, Akula II 1996, Yasen 2014, Yasen-M 2021), reusing the same-era pact torpedo, with real hull geometry in sub_specs.js so they get 3D models, and one AI line so the AI actually builds them. (3) render.js reads none of Threat.flash/.banner/.shake, so the 2D player hears three klaxons that differ only in pitch and sees nothing — rungs 2 and 3 are indistinguishable. I gave render.js its own drawThreat() plus a paint-space shake that deliberately does NOT move cam.ix/unproject, because ui.js turns clicks into tiles through those. (4) I am NOT marking the e20 unit default: rules.js's own comment says that roster really is present-day equipment, so contesting it is honest, and marking it would neutralise the e80-jammer-versus-2020s-radar contest the project deliberately made honest. The ERA_TIMELESS e50 default IS a fabrication by the file's own words ("what is being dated here is the role... not the rifle") and I marked that one. radarGen/jamGen is a genuine modelling gap but an owner decision — no edit, reasons below.

findings.what: closeInGuns() rejects every structure, so the AA Battery - the only gun air-defence emplacement in the game - can never contribute to the close-in intercept layer. It is separately (and correctly) excluded from the area layer because areaSam() requires proj==="missile". Net result: rules.js `flak` intercepts nothing at all, which is exactly what STATUS records as "zero on both intercept layers".
findings.evidence: js/combat.js:275 `if (e.dead || !e.owner || e.kind !== "unit") return;` inside closeInGuns; js/combat.js:233 `if (!w2 || !w2.tgt || !w2.tgt.air || w2.proj !== "missile") continue;` inside areaSam; js/rules.js:115 aa_battery is `proj:"shell"`; js/rules.js:236 flak is `cat:"defense"`, i.e. kind "building". The same function's comment at combat.js:265-271 argues guns belong here because "the land Phalanx is a 20mm gun" - which is a fixed emplacement.

findings.what: closeInGuns' unit test `!e.def.radar` cannot be applied to a structure: no BUILDINGS row carries a `radar` number except the Radar Dome itself, and on units def.radar is a RANGE IN TILES used by fog reveal and SEAD targeting. Giving `flak` a radar number to satisfy the gate would have made it lift fog and become a SEAD target - a far larger change than the fault. Powered-and-finished is the correct structural equivalent, and it is the test areaSam already applies.
findings.evidence: js/game.js:1744 `if (b.dead || !b.def.radar || b.buildProgress < 1 || !b.powered) continue;` then radarReveal(b, ..., b.def.radar); js/entities.js:1701 `if (sead) d *= (e.def && (e.def.radar || e.def.jam)) ? 0.06 : 6;`; js/combat.js:230 areaSam's own structure test `if (e.kind === "building" && (e.buildProgress < 1 || e.powered === false)) return;`

findings.what: Russia has no nuclear attack submarine anywhere. All five pact era hulls plus the present-day sub_p are diesel-electric; ssbn_p is a Borei and ssgn_p is an Oscar II, neither an SSN. The navy that built more SSNs than the rest of the world put together has none, while NATO has five.
findings.evidence: js/eras.js:9756/9775/9797/9820/9843 - pact_e50..e00_sub are Project 613 Whiskey, 641 Foxtrot, 877 Kilo, 636 Kilo, 636.3 Varshavyanka; js/rules.js:3055 `sub_p: { nuclear:false, ... }`. pact_e90_sub's own desc says "Project 971U Akula-II (Vepr, 1996) is the one genuinely modern nuclear boat of the [decade]" and pact_e00_sub's says "Project 885 Yasen (Severodvinsk, 2013) is the modern nuclear boat" - the file names the boats it does not contain.

findings.what: render.js does not read Threat at all. Threat.fire() distinguishes its rungs by KIND - rung 1 cue only, rung 2 amber flash + banner, rung 3 red flash + banner + shake - so with no visual channel the 2D renderer collapses rungs 2 and 3 into two klaxons that differ only in pitch, and a player with the window behind another cannot tell a wall being chewed from a refinery being lost.
findings.evidence: grep 'Threat' js/render.js returns one hit and it is a comment, js/render.js:1308. js/render3d.js:1588 `const k = Threat.shake;`, :2104 `const f = Threat.flash;`, :2116 `const b = Threat.banner;`. js/threat.js:183-192 fire() sets shake/flash/flashColor/banner and nothing else consumes them.

findings.what: The unit era default has TWO branches and only one is a fabrication. `_e.from = "e20"` is a claim the file explicitly stands behind ("Everything already in the roster is present-day equipment"), and marking it eraStamped would hand a flat x1.00 back to contests the project deliberately made honest. `ERA_TIMELESS -> e50` is a fabrication by the file's own admission and is unmarked, unlike the BUILDINGS loop ten lines below it which marks exactly this case.
findings.evidence: js/rules.js:4053-4058 (the two-branch loop) versus js/rules.js:4068 `if (_bb.from === undefined) { _bb.from = "e50"; _bb.eraStamped = true; }`; js/rules.js:4034-4038 "what is being dated here is the role, one team that removes individuals at distance... not the rifle"; js/game.js:913 is the only reader of eraStamped; js/rules.js:2707-2719 records that removing eraStamped from the E-2D was the RIGHT call once the date became real.

findings.what: The eraStamped fix for units has ZERO behavioural effect today and is a guard, not a repair - I checked all sixteen ERA_TIMELESS roles and not one unit in them carries radar, radarQ or jam, so none of them ever reaches genContest. Every undated sensor platform in the game is in the present-day rules.js roster and defaults to e20. This should be stated plainly rather than sold as a fixed number.
findings.evidence: Scanned every unit block in js/rules.js and js/eras.js for a role in ERA_TIMELESS carrying radar/radarQ/jam: none. The undated sensor platforms are all present-day rules.js rows - awacs_n/c/p/r (2599-2618), ew_n (2308), radarv_p (1149), spaag_r, spaag_g, sam_b, the fighters and the base subs - and every eras.js row carries an explicit "from".

findings.what: radarGen / jamGen is NOT a bug, it is a modelling gap, and it needs an owner decision rather than an edit from me. genContest keys off the platform's service era, which conflates the hull with the set inside it. awacs_n's own desc says so: "the APY-2 array itself dates from 1977 and Block 40/45 modernised the mission computers, not the radar" - yet a defaulted from:"e20" makes the E-3G a 2020s radar taking x0.166 from an e80 jammer. The engine change is one line (radarDef.radarGen || radarDef.from, jammerDef.jamGen || jammerDef.from); all the value is in the ~30 rows of data you would then have to author, and shipping the field with no data makes it dead code, which this codebase deliberately refuses to do. I have deliberately not written that edit.
findings.evidence: js/game.js:914-915 `const r = eraIndex(radarDef && radarDef.from ? radarDef.from : "e20"); const j = eraIndex(jammerDef && jammerDef.from ? jammerDef.from : "e20");`; js/rules.js:2602-2604 awacs_n desc; js/eras.js:10540 "genContest() reads it: the 1952 APS-20 below takes 1.7^3".

/* ==================================================================
   THE SOVIET AND RUSSIAN NUCLEAR ATTACK SUBMARINE

   Recorded as missing and it was. Every pact boat in this file is
   diesel-electric - Whiskey, Foxtrot, Kilo, Improved Kilo, Varshavyanka -
   and the present-day roster's sub_p is a Kilo as well, so the navy that
   built more nuclear attack submarines than the rest of the world put
   together had not one of them in any period. The hole was invisible
   because NATO's own `sub` role IS its SSN line - Nautilus, Sturgeon, Los
   Angeles, Seawolf, Virginia - so both navies had one submarine slot and
   the pact correctly spent its on the boat it had most of.

   THIS IS A SECOND ROLE, NOT A REPLACEMENT, because the Soviet Navy ran
   both lines side by side and the contrast is the point of having them:
   the Kilo is slow, short-legged and extremely quiet; the nuclear boat is
   fast, long-legged and - until 1984 - extremely loud. No faction without
   an `ssn` row loses anything, and none is given one to keep the sheet
   symmetrical: NATO's nuclear boats are already its `sub` role, and the
   PLA, the KPA and Taiwan are not handed a line they did not have.

   WHY THESE FIVE.
     e50  Project 627A November. K-3 Leninsky Komsomol commissioned 4 July
          1958, to the North Pole submerged in July 1962, thirteen hulls.
     e60  Project 671 Victor I. K-38 commissioned 5 November 1967, the
          first Soviet teardrop hull, one shaft, thirty-two knots.
     e80  Project 971 Shchuka-B, Akula I. K-284 commissioned 30 December
          1984 - the boat that ended the free ride. Project 945 Sierra
          commissioned the same year in titanium and only four were built,
          so the Akula is the class that belongs in the slot.
     e90  Project 971U Akula II. K-157 Vepr, 1996 - and pact_e90_sub's own
          desc already names it "the one genuinely modern nuclear boat"
          while the game had no such boat to build.
     e00  Project 885 Yasen. K-560 Severodvinsk, accepted 30 December 2013
          and in service 17 June 2014.
   The 2020s boat is ssn_p in rules.js, with the rest of the present day.

   THEY ARE LOUD AND THAT IS NOT A PENALTY. `quiet` is a signature and
   lower is harder to find. A November at 0.90 sits beside the Romeo's 1.00
   because the class was tracked across oceans; the Akula's 0.44 is the
   mid-1980s quieting leap, helped by the propeller milling machines sold
   through Toshiba and Kongsberg and by what the Walker ring handed over -
   a story nato_e80_sub's own desc already tells from the other side.

   NO LAND ATTACK BEFORE e00, which is the line the Kilo refit below draws
   and for the same reason: the S-10 Granat that Project 671RTM and the
   Akula could fire from 1987 was a nuclear-armed strategic round,
   withdrawn under the 1991 unilateral initiatives, and the conventional
   weapon is the Kalibr. So the Yasen carries tlam_p and the four boats
   before it carry torpedoes only.

   WEAPONS ARE THE SAME-ERA PACT TORPEDO and not a new id: one navy's
   nuclear and diesel boats in one decade fired the same 533 mm weapon, and
   generations.js clones a private per-unit copy of it regardless.
   ================================================================== */

Inserting a 60-line comment plus a five-unit Object.assign BETWEEN them leaves the header describing a table-driven refit block that no longer follows it, and puts five hand-written rows with unquoted keys under a header that says every row here is a generated one with a quoted key. Purely a documentation-integrity problem — the file still parses and reindexRoles() at 11422 still sees the units — but this file is unusually strict about its own headers.

fatals.problem: The combat.js replacement bakes a FALSE statement about this codebase into a permanent comment, and the whole justification for the edit's shape rests on it. It says "no structure in the table has that field - on a unit it is a fog-lifting RANGE IN TILES, and giving the battery one would have made it reveal map and draw SEAD", and finding #2 says "no BUILDINGS row carries a `radar` number except the Radar Dome itself". Both are wrong. js/rules.js lines 1502-1505 read: BUILDINGS.radar.radar = 22; BUILDINGS.airbase.radar = 11; BUILDINGS.sam.radar = 15; BUILDINGS.flak.radar = 9;  The AA Battery ALREADY carries radar 9, so it ALREADY lifts fog (game.js:1744 walks G.human.buildings on `b.def.radar` and calls radarReveal with it) and ALREADY draws SEAD (entities.js:1701 tests `e.def.radar || e.def.jam` on both kinds). The stated reason for exempting structures from the radar gate does not exist, and the false comment would sit forty lines from the code that disproves it.

The render.js shake detaches the world-space overlay from the world. The replacement puts drawOverlay(input) AFTER ctx.restore(), on the stated theory that "the shake stops at the HUD" - but drawOverlay is not a HUD. It is a mixed layer: drawRangeRings() (render.js:1179, called at 1234) paints weapon envelopes through sx()/sy(); the building-placement ghost paints its tiles with `const X = sx(wx, wy), Y = sy(wx, wy, e)`; the build-radius ellipses use sx(b.x, b.y); the rally flags use sx(b.rally.x, b.rally.y). All four are world space. With the world layer translated by up to 9 px and drawOverlay untranslated, during a tier-3 shake the range rings, the placement ghost, the build-radius circles and the rally flags slide visibly off the units and buildings they annotate - and a tier-3 shake fires on a structure being LOST, which is exactly when the player is siting a rebuild. The 3D path has no such problem because it shakes the camera (render3d.js:2101-2115 applyShake), so everything projected moves together under a genuinely screen-space overlay. The plan's own measurement #5 would pass and miss this: input.placeTx/placeTy are indeed unchanged, because unproject() is unshaken - the tile index is right and the picture is wrong.
fatals.correction: Either (a) put the world-space half inside the shake: call drawRangeRings() and a split-out drawPlaceGhost(input) / rally-flag pass immediately before `ctx.restore();`, and leave only the drag-selection rectangle and the attack-move cursor (both pure input.mx/input.my) in drawOverlay after it; or (b) - smaller and cleaner - drop the outer ctx.save()/translate()/restore() entirely and fold the offset into the projection instead: `function sx(wx, wy) { return (isoX(wx, wy) - cam.ix) * cam.z + W / 2 + shX; }` and the matching `+ shY` in sy(), plus `+ shX`/`+ shY` on the two explicit `ctx.translate(-cam.ix - ox, -cam.iy - 20)` calls (the terrain blit in draw() and the one in drawFog()). unproject() is deliberately left untouched in (b), which preserves the click-to-tile guarantee the plan wanted while keeping every world-space mark glued to the world. Option (b) also removes the 9 px band of bare "#07090c" that the current version exposes at the shaken edges, since the background fillRect happens before the translate.
